LESSON: THE BIRTH AND CHILDHOOD OF JESUS CHRIST

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Early Life of Jesus Christ
Topic 4.3: The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do Christians celebrate the birth of Jesus Christ?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the dedication of baby Jesus
2. identify values learnt from the birth and childhood of Jesus Christ

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: THE BIRTH AND CHILDHOOD OF JESUS CHRIST
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: THE BIRTH AND CHILDHOOD OF JESUS CHRIST
Study The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the dedication of baby Jesus

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the dedication of baby Jesus. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the dedication of baby Jesus.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the dedication of baby Jesus. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify values learnt from the birth and childhood of Jesus Christ

What this means
In this part you learn to identify values learnt from the birth and childhood of Jesus Christ. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify values learnt from the birth and childhood of Jesus Christ.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify values learnt from the birth and childhood of Jesus Christ. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the dedication of baby Jesus)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ in your own words. (skill: identify values learnt from the birth and childhood of Jesus Christ)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the dedication of baby Jesus.
3. Practise this skill: identify values learnt from the birth and childhood of Jesus Christ.
4. Make one local Kenya example of The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do Christians celebrate the birth of Jesus Christ?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what The Birth and Childhood of Jesus Christ means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the dedication of baby Jesus.
5. Be able to: identify values learnt from the birth and childhood of Jesus Christ.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
